pack_tagline: Ten AI skills that take real work off an e-commerce team's plate: photos, listings, profit, cash on delivery, stock and conversion. Install one in a minute, answer a few setup questions once, and reuse it every week.

skills.title: Catalog photos from a *mannequin shot*
skills.tagline: Turn raw product photos into a consistent, professional catalog shoot with the same AI model every time.
does: Replaces the mannequin, hanger or flat lay with a real-looking model wearing the identical garment
Handles non-clothing too: a model holding your perfume or phone case, or clean studio and lifestyle packshots
Keeps one house model, background and light across every shoot, so the store looks like one brand
Compares every result with your original photo and redoes anything that changed the product
setup: What you sell and the model's look: gender, age, body type, skin tone, hair
Modesty level, including a hijab option, and default footwear
Your house model: pick from 4 generated faces or upload your own (with consent)
Default background, photo shape and a credit limit per run
try: Here is my folder of new arrivals. Make catalog photos for all of them.
Put this abaya on our house model, front and back, white background.
Make a lifestyle shot of this perfume on a marble bathroom shelf.
get: Store-ready images named by colour and view (black-front.png)
A quality report: what was redone and why
An optional hand-off to the Shopify upload skill
skills.safety: Only your own photos and faces you have consent for. Modest and kids rules are enforced on every image. Credits are quoted before big runs.

skills.title: From photo folder to *live listings*
skills.tagline: Upload finished product photos to Shopify as complete, correct listings, or add new colours to products you already sell.
does: Creates one product per folder with every colour and size as a variant, photos linked to each colour
Writes titles and descriptions from the photos, in English, Arabic or both
Numbers SKUs in your store's own pattern and links colour swatches so they show on collection pages
Builds each product as a draft, checks it, and only then publishes it
setup: Confirms your store, then reads your recent products to detect your SKU and title style
Charge taxes, sell when out of stock, and which sales channels to publish to
Copy language and brand voice
Go live after checks, or leave as drafts for you to review
try: Upload the products in this folder. Prices and stock are in this sheet.
These are two new colours of the Linen Midi Dress. Add them as variants.
Give me a sheet to fill in with prices and sizes for these products.
get: Live (or draft) products with variants, SKUs, photos, swatches and collections
A store link and admin link for every product
An upload log you can rerun safely without duplicates
skills.safety: Nothing is written until you approve the full plan. Products stay hidden until verified. Nothing is ever deleted.

skills.title: Find where cash on delivery *goes wrong*
skills.tagline: See which areas, couriers, products and customers refuse or return COD orders, what it costs you, and what to change.
does: Groups COD orders by governorate and city (English, Arabic and Franco spellings), courier, product, order value and customer history
Calculates delivery success, failure rate and money lost to failed deliveries
Reads optional courier exports from any courier to get real statuses and fees
Turns the numbers into actions, like deposits for one area or confirming orders above a value
needs: Shopify connector or an orders export
setup: Your couriers, and how you mark a failed or refused order in Shopify
The cost of one failed delivery, if no courier file has it
COD orders only or all orders, and the minimum sample before ranking
Report, dashboard or spreadsheet
try: Analyse my COD failures for the last 3 months. Here is my Bosta export too.
Which governorates should I ask for a deposit?
How much did failed deliveries cost me last month?
get: The worst areas and segments, ranked only when the sample is big enough
The cost of failed deliveries per month
Concrete actions with an estimated saving, clearly labelled as estimates
skills.safety: Read only. Nothing in your store changes. Estimates always state their assumptions.

skills.title: What every product *really* earns you
skills.tagline: Real profit per product, order and channel after ads, shipping, COD fees, failed deliveries, returns and payment fees.
does: Combines Shopify orders with Meta, TikTok and Google Ads exports, courier files and supplier invoices
Splits ad spend to products by your campaigns, or by revenue share when campaigns are mixed
Shows contribution profit, margin and break-even ROAS for every product
Flags the bestsellers that actually lose money
needs: Shopify connector or an orders export
Optional: ads and courier exports, supplier invoices
setup: Where your product costs live and whether prices include VAT
Payment fees, courier COD fees, shipping and packaging costs
Optional fixed monthly costs
How to split ad spend, and the exchange rate if your ad account uses another currency
try: Here are my Meta and TikTok exports for October. Which products make money?
What is my break-even ROAS per product?
Read these supplier invoices and update my product costs.
get: Profit per product, per order and per channel
A list of bestsellers that lose money, with why
A dashboard where you can test new prices, ad budgets and costs
skills.safety: Read only. Products without a cost show as unknown, never as zero. Every assumption is written down.

skills.title: Your business on *one page*, every week
skills.tagline: A weekly snapshot of sales, customers, COD delivery, returns and stock, compared with last week, with three things to act on.
does: Tracks net sales, orders, average order value, new vs returning customers and top and bottom products
Follows COD share, delivery success, refunds and stock that is about to run out
Compares with last week and four weeks ago, and flags real changes only
Runs on a schedule in agents that support it, with no questions asked
needs: Shopify connector or an orders export
setup: Timezone and the day your week starts
Which KPIs to show, and your weekly targets
How you record a failed COD delivery
Format, language, delivery (file, chat or email draft) and the weekly schedule
try: Give me last week's digest.
Set this up to run every Saturday at 9.
Why did net sales drop this week?
get: A one-page report, dashboard or spreadsheet
Week-over-week changes that matter, with plain explanations
Exactly three things to act on
skills.safety: Read only. Missing data, like sessions, is shown as missing, never estimated. Emails are drafts until you send them.

skills.title: Size charts customers *can trust*
skills.tagline: Build accurate, bilingual size charts from supplier sheets or your own measurements, ready for the product page.
does: Reads supplier spec sheets, photos of measured garments or numbers you type
Checks for mistakes: sizes that shrink, missing sizes and uneven grading
Converts centimetres and inches, and turns flat garment measurements into body guidance
Renders a mobile-friendly table in English, Arabic (right to left) or both
needs: Optional: Shopify connector to place the chart
setup: Main unit, languages and Arabic digit style
Size labels you use and the categories you sell
How your brand fits, and whether numbers describe the garment or the body
Where charts live: description, a shared page, a metafield or an app
try: Here is the factory spec sheet. Make a size chart for this dress in English and Arabic.
Check this size chart for mistakes.
Add this chart to all products in the Dresses collection.
get: A clean HTML size chart with a how-to-measure guide and fit note
A list of problems found in your numbers
The chart placed in your store, only after you approve
skills.safety: Store changes only after you confirm the exact list. Standard tables are labelled as starting points, not truth.

skills.title: Why customers *send it back*
skills.tagline: Turn return notes in English, Arabic and Franco-Arabic into a clear list of products to fix and how.
does: Reads Shopify returns, refunds, order notes and returns app or support chat exports
Sorts reasons like too small, too large, quality, not as pictured, wrong item and late delivery
Calculates return rates per product, size and colour, and the money lost
Keeps refused COD orders separate from real returns
needs: Shopify connector or an orders export
Optional: returns app or chat exports
setup: Your return window, and how you mark returns, exchanges and refused orders
What a return shipment and an exchange cost you
Reasons or customer words you want tracked differently
Minimum sales before judging a product, format and language
try: Why are customers returning the oversized hoodie?
Which products should I fix first to cut returns?
Analyse these return notes from WhatsApp.
get: The top products to fix, with the specific fix (size chart, photos, supplier quality)
Return rates by product, size and colour
Trends over time, and exchanges vs refunds
skills.safety: Read only. Small samples are not ranked. Reasons the skill is unsure about are confirmed with you.

skills.title: Reorder at the right time, *in the right amount*
skills.tagline: Predicts demand for every variant and tells you when to reorder and how much, without tying up more cash than needed.
does: Reads your sales and stock, weighting recent weeks more and skipping days you were out of stock
Plans for Ramadan, Eid and White Friday when there is enough history
Uses your supplier lead time, minimum order and case pack to size each order
Shows the trade-off between fewer stockouts and cash tied in stock
needs: Shopify connector or orders and inventory exports
setup: Supplier lead time, how reliable it is, and how often you reorder
How often you want to have stock when a customer orders (service level)
Minimum order quantities and case packs
Where unit costs live, and your output format
try: What do I need to reorder this week?
Plan my stock for Ramadan.
How much cash do I have tied up in stock?
get: A reorder list: what, when, how much and the cash needed
Items at risk of running out, with their stockout dates
A dashboard where you can change lead time and service level
skills.safety: Read only. New products and short histories are flagged as estimates. Missing costs show as unknown.

skills.title: Turn more visitors into *orders*
skills.tagline: Audits your storefront for what stops people buying, then fixes it on a copy of your theme with your OK.
does: Checks speed, mobile layout, product pages, trust signals, checkout friction, navigation, SEO and Arabic quality
Shows evidence for every problem and ranks fixes by impact and effort
Fixes theme issues on a duplicate theme you preview before anything goes live
Edits content like descriptions and alt text in small batches you approve
needs: Optional: Shopify connector or Shopify CLI for fixes
setup: Store URL, languages, main market and currency
How changes can be made: CLI, connector or manual steps for you
What it may change, and what to focus on first
Brand voice, Arabic style and report format
try: Audit my store for conversion problems.
Fix the top five issues on a copy of my theme.
Is my product page clear about delivery time and COD?
get: A prioritised fix list with a health score per area
A preview link of the fixed theme copy
A change log you can roll back
skills.safety: Never edits your live theme. Every batch of changes needs your yes. Every change is logged for rollback.

skills.title: Free the cash stuck in *slow stock*
skills.tagline: Finds slow and dead stock and the cash locked in it, then plans how to clear it without killing your margin.
does: Classifies every variant as healthy, slow or dead by last sale, days of cover and sell-through
Shows the cash stuck in slow and dead stock
Proposes a tactic per item: markdown, bundle with a bestseller, free gift, clearance collection or liquidation
Keeps every markdown above your minimum margin
needs: Shopify connector or orders, products and inventory exports
setup: When an item counts as slow and when it counts as dead
Your lowest acceptable margin, and whether to allow below-cost clearance
Markdown steps, price rounding and the tactics you allow
Clearance tag and collection names, and your output format
try: What stock is not selling, and how much cash is stuck in it?
Plan a clearance for items with no sale in 90 days.
Apply the markdowns we agreed on.
get: A clearance plan with the cash you can recover
A change list (prices, tags, collections) you review before anything happens
A rollback file with the old values
skills.safety: No store change without your yes on the exact list. Old prices are saved before any change, so it can be undone.
